title: Mastering Strong Collocations
summary: Learn how certain English words naturally go together to sound more fluent. You will study useful combinations with rain, decisions, and risks.

sections.p: In English, some words love to hang out together. We call these strong collocations. If you use the wrong word, native speakers will understand you, but it will sound a little strange. For example, we do not say 'big rain' or 'do a decision'. Learning these fixed pairs helps your speaking and writing sound much more natural and confident at a B2 level.

ex.en: We use certain words together because it sounds natural.
ex.mean: Some words are partners in English.

ex.en: Using correct collocations helps you sound like a native speaker.
ex.mean: Right word partnerships make you sound fluent.

sections.p: Let us look at weather and choices. When it is raining a lot, we never say 'strong rain'. The natural collocation is 'heavy rain'. Also, when you need to choose something important, the correct verb is not 'do', it is 'make'. You 'make a decision'. Try to memorize these phrases as whole chunks instead of learning the words separately.

ex.en: We had to stay inside because of the heavy rain.
ex.mean: We stayed indoors due to the very bad rain.

ex.en: Take your time to make a decision about the job offer.

sections.p: Finally, let us talk about doing brave things. In English, we do not 'make a risk' or 'do a risk'. We always 'take a risk'. Business owners and athletes often have to take risks to succeed. Learning these verbs with their correct noun partners will stop you from translating directly from your native language.

ex.en: Sometimes you need to take a risk to achieve your goals.
ex.mean: You must do something risky to succeed.

ex.en: She was afraid to take a risk, so she stayed in her safe job.
ex.mean: She avoided danger and kept her safe job.

tip: Do not learn words alone. Always write down the full phrase, like 'take a risk', so your brain remembers them as a team.

quiz.ask: Choose the correct collocation for bad weather.
quiz.en: We got completely wet in the ___ rain.

quiz.ask: Choose the correct verb for a choice.
quiz.en: It is hard to ___ a decision when you have too many options.

quiz.ask: Choose the correct phrase for doing something brave.
quiz.en: Starting a new business means you have to ___.
Please don't forget to ___ before Friday.

quiz.ask: Which adjective goes with 'rain' in English?
quiz.en: The match was cancelled because of ___ rain.

quiz.ask: Choose the correct verb for this phrase.
quiz.en: Are you willing to ___ a risk to win the competition?
